candidates.label: E2 early B+zombie merge
candidates.change: B only: zombie_entry mov bp,3400h -> 09400h (b/d, CX=0 path) and mov bp,2000h -> 06800h (zom20a, CX!=0 path). Two immediates (B bytes 0x40/0x44). Zombie anchors move out of B's own 3Ch-page band window (removes the B059 self-kill) and the same-step zombie stream lands on B's anchor after a 2 (zom20a) / 3 (b/d) generation lead, so B and its zombies merge early and stay merged.

threatFindings.threat: Structural SP/anchor residue misalignment in some stream (A, B, captured zombies) causing rebuild failures
threatFindings.evidence: Static: all streams use AL=A2h with FAR_SEG 0FFBh -> anchor in-page 52h (=2 mod 4), pages = band+phase with band a multiple of 3Ch and phases 2Ch/10h/20h/34h (all = 0 mod 4) -> one shared 400h lattice; SP-anchor = 150h (A) / 650h (B, zombies) in gen 0 and BP-DX = 400h/800h later, all multiples of 4, also across 64K wraparound. Trace pkj3o (base): 243 of 267 deaths of our code have SP = 2 mod 4. The 24 exceptions are all external: FF CC (= dec sp) after CC bombs on the anchor (fisherEXE, KosherCode), sliding through a 0024h-bombed region into own trail bytes (A4 44 = movsb; inc sp), and opponent-corrupted startup immediates (one A with DX=E000h and odd SP, one A with T=B7E9h whose trail trigger byte became EB instead of A4). Scripts: agent2/night/scratch/A016/align3.mjs, spmis.mjs, gen.mjs.
threatFindings.impact: No alignment fix needed; residues are correct by construction.

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombie's first anchor stosw (FF 1F) lands in B's not-yet-run startup code (zombie phases 20h/34h are inside B's own band window)
threatFindings.evidence: Trace pkj3o: s2025-1 war 2 r47 CAND2 jumps to CS 0000 (B load 97BCh, band 78h, zom20a anchor page 98h = arena 9852h inside B's code) and war 15 r56 CAND2 calls its still-CC anchor with AX=T (B load 33A3h, b/d anchor arena 3452h inside B's code). Absent in E2 trace wp7fs (phases 68h/94h). Same finding as B059.
threatFindings.impact: About 2-3 of 161 deaths; any zombie phase >= 40h pages avoids it.

threatFindings.threat: Same-step B and captured-zombie streams merge onto one anchor (zombie at speed 2 gains about 1 generation per B generation and lands on B's anchor when its lead = m mod 64, m = 35*(P-10h)/4 mod 64 with P = zombie phase in pages; base zom20a m=12, b/d m=59)
threatFindings.evidence: pkj3o (base): 5 joint same-anchor deaths of CAND2 and zom20a at r7967-9420 (F8A3h/D0A3h), as predicted for m=12. wp7fs (E2, m=2/3): 26 joint same-anchor death groups at r~1000-5000, and 17 dwell deaths whose anchor FF was written by another of our streams (vs 6 in base).
threatFindings.impact: The merge time is set by the zombie phases alone and is a usable design parameter.

threatFindings.threat: Merging hurts because one anchor hit kills B and its zombie together
threatFindings.evidence: E2 (early merge) has 5x more joint deaths but fewer B deaths (73 vs 80) and fewer total deaths (150 vs 161) in trace wp7fs, and screen dbb6r +0.020; the late-merge contrast L63 is -0.014 (9eoj2). Early merge helping is a hypothesis: E2 +0.020 and E4 +0.017 (4mpph) both positive, but each CI includes 0 and placement edits on field S have a half-width of about 0.03.
threatFindings.impact: If confirmed, earlier zombie-B merge is a cheap two-immediate lever; zph (zom20a lead 25, b/d lead 8) and zph2 (9, 56) fit the same picture only loosely.

threatFindings.threat: Corruption of B's arena worker template before copying kills B and both captured zombies at their first rebuild (all three copy the template from B's code)
threatFindings.evidence: pkj3o: sthreat-movsw_TrojanByte war 15: zom20a r256, zom20d r260, CAND2 r483 all die at T+17h executing trail bytes after a 2-byte (not 4-byte) push; s2025-2 war 2: CAND2 r481 and zom20a r252 both die with SI=13h, DI=T1-1 on a never-written new anchor (xor si,si and stosw were not executed). Who wrote into the template could not be identified (hypothesis: opponent or zombie writes in the first ~25 rounds).
threatFindings.impact: Rare (2 events per 160 battles). A fix would need a second template source; not attempted.

recommendation: Send E2 (agent2/night/scratch/A016/E2_B.asm, B sha 229e1588..., A = base) to confirmation as a promising candidate: screen ALL +0.0201 [-0.0113,+0.0515], no clearly negative group (multi -0.003), and the trace shows the intended mechanism (early B+zombie merge, B059 self-kill gone, fewer B deaths). Caution: this is a placement edit like zph, whose screen +0.037 shrank to +0.009 in confirmation; E4 (+0.017, multi -0.019) is a replication with other phases, and L63 (-0.014) is the late-merge contrast. If E2 does not confirm, the merge-lead model (m = 35*(P-10h)/4 mod 64) is still useful for choosing zombie phases in combinations with fix2steal/A003 C1. No structural SP/anchor misalignment exists in rev0.
notes: Screens were against rev0 = current base. bytes[] in trace records start at IP-4 (IP is after the faulting instruction), at least for these traces; 'hist' gives the last 24 rounds of A/B registers.
